name: J. L. Truscott
role: Rancher; secretary of stockmen's association; chairman of Billings County commissioners
bio: J. L. Truscott was a Little Missouri cattleman who took part in the Bad Lands stockmen's meeting of March 1884 and came in from Beaver creek at the close of the district's first round-up that June. He was among the ranchers who called a stockmen's meeting in December 1884, and in spring 1885 he was elected secretary of the Little Missouri River Stockgrowers' Association. In July 1885 his bride, the former Maggie Gardient, arrived in Medora, and in December 1885 the paper reported the birth of a daughter at the Spring creek ranch. Elected a Billings County commissioner in 1886, he was chosen chairman of the board in May and presided over meetings on liquor licenses and county bills. In August 1886 the stockgrowers named him to represent them at Bismarck if cattle legislation was needed, and that fall he was nominated again for commissioner.
